correctness.rationale: The valuation identity follows directly from factoring out the common minimum \(p\)-valuation. On the primitive layer, goodness is the union of nonzero coordinate sum and the all-nonzero zero-sum configurations; the latter count is the standard additive-character value \(((p-1)^k+(p-1)(-1)^k)/p\). Common-divisibility layers contribute \((p-1)/(p(p^k-1))\). CRT gives the finite-prime product, while the large-prime obstruction is bounded by \(\sum_{p>Y}p^{-k}\) plus a union bound of order \(1/Y\) for primitive tuples. Thus the cutoff can be removed. The local bad mass is \(O_k(p^{-2})\), giving a positive convergent Euler product. Fresh counts for \(k=2,3,4\) and \(p=2,3,5\) reproduced the character count and local factors.

final_claim: For every fixed \(k\ge2\), the box density of tuples with \(\gcd(a_1\cdots a_k,a_1+\cdots+a_k)/\gcd(a_1,\ldots,a_k)=1\) exists and equals \(\prod_p c_{k,p}\), where \(c_{k,p}=1-1/p+((p-1)^k+(p-1)(-1)^k)/p^{k+1}+(p-1)/(p(p^k-1))\); the product is positive and recovers the known pair factor.
limitations: Fixed \(k\) and ordinary box density only; no effective error term or higher distribution is claimed.
